comment: Mutation testing for the SHIPPED RUNTIME assembly. A THIRD config because Stryker mutates one 'project' per run. Registry members, MapConfig, the IDwarfMapper facade and the exception types have no derivable case-space the way an attribute does — there is no AttributeUsage to decompose and no endpoint matrix to cross them against — so a surviving mutant is the only non-textual proof that a case is untested. This is what makes AmbiguousInterfaces and DestinationType (zero references in any test family, round 18) impossible rather than merely noticed. test-projects is DELIBERATELY not DwarfMapper.Generator.Tests: that project's references to the runtime types are overwhelmingly assertions over EMITTED SOURCE TEXT, not executions of this assembly, and its one genuine runtime executor (AutoValidateRuntimeTests) exercises Register/IsProvided paths that IntegrationTests already drives directly — at a fraction of the wall-clock. The one thing that exclusion does cost: DwarfMapValidationException is thrown only by GENERATED code (AmbientValidator), and AutoValidateRuntimeTests is the only test that runs a generated validator, so nothing here reaches it. Measured cost is nevertheless ZERO — its three constructors are bare ': base(...)' forwarders and Stryker produced no mutants for them at all (2026-08-16 run: every mutant in DwarfMapExceptions.cs falls in DwarfMapMissingException, lines 40-107). Recheck that if the type ever grows logic. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker). MEASURED 2026-08-16 on Stryker 4.16.0: score 66.95 % (79 killed-or-timed-out of 118 scoreable; 32 survived, 7 uncovered, 8 compile errors excluded), 44 min wall-clock on 12 cores. break is that score rounded DOWN to 66 — a ratchet, raised as survivors are killed and never lowered without a deliberate edit. NOTE 1: 'comment' lives OUTSIDE the 'stryker-config' object because Stryker 4.16 REJECTS unknown keys inside it — the two sibling configs kept theirs inside and could not run at all until this was found. NOTE 2: the 'mutate' globs must NOT be repo-root-relative. Stryker resolves them against the PROJECT directory (src/DwarfMapper), so 'src/DwarfMapper/Foo.cs' matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0 — a vacuous run that housekeeping's $LASTEXITCODE check cannot detect. That is exactly what the first measured run of this file did.
